metadata.provenance: 57 real tool definitions from local endpoint snapshots for servers found in local catalog events; 24 hand-written modelled tools on BlogCMS, StartupMarket and ProductDirectory. No customer call arguments or results.
metadata.labels: Hand-labelled before evaluation. expect lists all required tools, not interchangeable alternatives. Missing arguments may require clarification; labels identify capabilities, not executable calls.
metadata.zero_overlap: No alphanumeric token overlap with the expected tool name, key or full description; includes stopwords. Input schemas are not part of the evaluator ranking text.
metadata.limitations: Constructed diagnostic set, not sampled production traffic. Category proportions do not estimate real-world frequencies. Modelled tools are illustrative, not claimed vendor contracts.

catalog.name: get_page_data
catalog.description: Fetch live data for every widget on a page you own, concurrently. Returns an array of { widget_id, label, kind, data }. Static kinds (links, badges) are included and resolve cheaply from config.

catalog.name: get_weekly_recap
catalog.description: The current weekly recap (week-over-week growth of public headline metrics) for a page you own. Returns null when nothing grew in the window.

catalog.name: get_widget_data
catalog.description: Fetch the current live data for one widget on a page you own. Kind, label, and credential are read from the stored widget — you cannot pass them, so no other user's integration secrets can be reached. Returns the widget's data JSON.

widget_id.description: The widget ID (as listed by list_widgets).

catalog.name: get_widget_history
catalog.description: Daily metric history for one widget on a page you own, newest first. 'days' defaults to 30, capped at 365. Each point has recorded_at, value, metric_kind, label, currency, and any chartable series.

days.description: Days of history to return (default 30, capped at 365).

widget_id.description: The widget ID (as listed by list_widgets).

catalog.name: list_pages

catalog.name: list_widgets

catalog.name: create_changelog_entry
catalog.description: Create a changelog entry on the project's public board changelog. 'title' is required; 'body' is Markdown. Optional 'version' (e.g. v1.4.0), 'category' (one of: added, improved, fixed, changed, removed, security), and 'component' (a slug from the project's component registry naming the product asset the entry belongs to, e.g. 'cli' or 'react-sdk' — keep 'version' a pure version and use 'component' for the asset instead of encoding it into the version string; an unknown slug errors listing the valid ones). By default the entry lands as a draft for review; set 'publish' to true to publish it to the public board immediately (published entries are included in the changelog email digest to subscribers). Optional 'published_at' (RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD) backdates the display date — use it when importing existing changelog history. Returns the created entry.

publish.description: Publish to the public board immediately instead of leaving as a draft

version.description: Optional version/tag shown as a badge (e.g. "v1.4.0")

category.description: Optional category: added, improved, fixed, changed, removed, or security

component.description:
Optional component slug from the project's registry (e.g. "cli",
"react-sdk") — which product asset this entry belongs to. An unknown
slug errors with the valid slugs.

published_at.description:
Explicit display date (RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD) — backdate entries when
importing existing changelog history. Defaults to the publish moment.

- star: value is 1-5 (or 1-max_stars if specified)

path.description: URL path where the rating relates to

value.description:
Rating value (meaning depends on type):
- helpful: true/false as 1/0
- star: 1-5 (or 1-max_stars)
- nps: 0-10

version.description: Application version to track ratings against specific releases

max_stars.description: Maximum stars (only for star type, defaults to 5)

rating_type.description: Rating type: helpful, star, or nps

submitted_by.description: User identifier who submitted the rating

catalog.name: delete_rating
catalog.description: Delete a rating item. This performs a soft-delete (archive) - the item is not permanently removed.

catalog.name: get_rating

catalog.name: get_survey

Get aggregated statistics for any rating type. Response varies by type:

- nps: total, score (-100 to 100), promoters, passives, detractors, distribution
Required: project_id. Optional: rating_type (defaults to helpful), path.

rating_type.description: Rating type: helpful, star, or nps (defaults to helpful)

catalog.name: list_changelog
catalog.description: List all changelog entries for a project (every status: draft, published, hidden), newest first. Each entry has a source (manual, github_release, completed_idea), title, Markdown body, optional version, category, and component (a slug naming the product asset, e.g. 'cli'), and lifecycle status. Optional 'component' narrows to one component slug. Call this before creating an entry to avoid duplicates.

component.description: Optional component slug to narrow the list (e.g. "cli", "react-sdk")

catalog.name: list_feedback
catalog.description: List feedback items for a project. Supports pagination (page, limit) and filtering by status (New/Active/Assigned/Hold/Closed/Resolved), type (Bug/Feature/Praise/Question/Improvement/Other), and search term.

type.description: Filter by type: Bug, Feature, Praise, Question, Improvement, Other

limit.description: Number of items per page (1-100, defaults to 20)

search.description: Search term to filter feedback by message content

status.description: Filter by status: New, Active, Assigned, Hold, Closed, Resolved

catalog.name: list_ideas
catalog.description: List ideas (feature requests) for a project. Returns compact rows: id, title, status, votes_count, comments_count, completed_in_version, created_at, plus pagination. Optional 'status' filter (Pending, Open, Planned, Started, Completed, Declined, Duplicate, Rejected; omit for all), 'sort' ('votes' = most voted first, 'newest' = default), 'search' (title/description), 'page', 'limit' (1-100, default 20). The public roadmap is the Planned, Started and Completed ideas. Use get_idea for the description, admin response and linked GitHub issue.

limit.description: Number of items per page (1-100, defaults to 20)

search.description: Search term matched against title and description

status.description: Filter by status: Pending, Open, Planned, Started, Completed, Declined, Duplicate, Rejected (omit for all)

catalog.name: list_projects
catalog.description: List all projects for your organization. Returns project details including name, description, allowed origins, and feedback count.

catalog.name: list_ratings
catalog.description: List ratings (thumbs up/down) for a project. Supports pagination (page, limit) and filtering by path and value (true=helpful, false=not helpful).

limit.description: Number of items per page (1-100, defaults to 20)

value.description: Filter by value (true for helpful, false for not helpful)

catalog.name: list_surveys
catalog.description: List all surveys for a project. Returns each survey's full definition (questions, trigger, status, display mode) plus its response count. Survey statuses: draft, live, paused, archived.

catalog.name: merge_ideas
catalog.description: Merge a duplicate idea ('source_id') into the canonical idea to keep ('target_id'), both in the same project. Votes move to the target (a voter who backed both counts once), comments move with them, and the source becomes status Duplicate with merged_into_id pointing at the target; it stays visible on the public board as a merged duplicate. Cannot be undone through the API. The source must not already be a Duplicate, and the target must not itself be merged away. To merge several duplicates, call once per duplicate. Returns votes_migrated, votes_deduplicated and comments_migrated.

source_id.description: The duplicate idea to merge away (becomes Duplicate)

target_id.description: The canonical idea to keep (receives the votes and comments)

catalog.name: report_problem
catalog.description: Report a bug, docs mismatch, friction or missing feature you hit while using this MCP server or the SeggWat API. The report goes to the SeggWat team, not to your projects. One report per distinct problem; keep working after filing. 'category' must be one of: bug, docs_mismatch, friction, feature_gap, quality_degradation, other. 'surface' is the MCP tool name or API path you were using.

type.description: One of: http_summary, stderr_excerpt, repro_steps, screenshot, log_excerpt, other

content.description: The evidence itself, e.g. the error message or request/response summary

ReportEvidenceInput.description: One evidence item for a problem report

title.description: One-line summary of the problem (max 256 characters)

summary.description: What happened versus what you expected (max 4096 characters)

surface.description: What you were using: an MCP tool name (e.g. list_feedback) or an API path (e.g. GET /api/v1/projects)

category.description: One of: bug, docs_mismatch, friction, feature_gap, quality_degradation, other

evidence.description: Up to 10 evidence items (max 65536 bytes each)

severity.description: One of: critical, high, medium, low (defaults to medium)

catalog.name: set_changelog_status
catalog.description: Change a changelog entry's lifecycle status. 'status' must be one of: draft, published, hidden. 'published' puts the entry live on the public board changelog — this is the review gate for drafts from GitHub-release sync and completed ideas. 'draft' unpublishes; 'hidden' soft-hides without deleting. Publishing also makes the entry eligible for the subscriber email digest, and the first publish of an entry created from feedback emails the original submitter. Returns the updated entry.

status.description: New status: draft, published, or hidden

catalog.name: set_survey_status
catalog.description: Change a survey's lifecycle status. The 'status' must be one of: draft, live, paused, archived. Setting a survey to 'live' is what makes it fire from the widget. Returns the updated survey.

status.description: New status: draft, live, paused, or archived

catalog.name: setup_project
catalog.description: Set up SeggWat feedback for a codebase in one call: creates the project, or returns the existing one with the same name, so it is safe to re-run. Returns the widget install snippet per framework (html, nextjs, nuxt) and the project key. Add exactly one snippet to the layout rendered on every page, then submit a test feedback through the widget and call verify_setup. Fails with a billing link when the organization has no active trial or has reached its plan's project limit.

name.description:
Project name, usually the app or site name. An existing project with this name
(case-insensitive) is returned instead of creating a duplicate.

allowed_origins.description:
Origins allowed to load the widget, e.g. `["https://example.com"]`. Pass the site's
production origin(s); omitted allows every origin (`*`). Ignored for an existing project.

catalog.name: update_changelog_entry
catalog.description: Update a changelog entry's content: title, Markdown body, version, category, component. Only the fields you pass change; omitted fields keep their current value (pass an empty string to clear 'version', 'category', or 'component'). Works on any entry regardless of status — use it to polish synced GitHub-release or completed-idea drafts before publishing. Returns the updated entry.

body.description: New Markdown body (omit to keep the current one)

title.description: New title (omit to keep the current one)

version.description: New version badge, e.g. "v1.4.0" (omit to keep the current one; pass "" to clear)

category.description: New category: added, improved, fixed, changed, removed, or security (omit to keep; pass "" to clear)

component.description: New component slug from the project's registry (omit to keep; pass "" to clear)

catalog.name: update_feedback
catalog.description: Update a feedback item. At least one field must be provided: message, type (Bug/Feature/Praise/Question/Improvement/Other), status (New/Active/Assigned/Hold/Closed/Resolved), or resolution_note. Setting status to Resolved emails the feedback submitter (when they left an email and the project has resolution emails enabled); a resolution_note is included in that email.

type.description: Updated type: Bug, Feature, Praise, Question, Improvement, Other

status.description: Updated status: New, Active, Assigned, Hold, Closed, Resolved

resolution_note.description: Optional note from the team when resolving feedback (included in resolution email to submitter)

catalog.name: update_idea
catalog.description: Update an idea (feature request). Provide at least one of: 'status' (Pending, Open, Planned, Started, Completed, Declined, Rejected — use merge_ideas for duplicates), 'completed_in_version' (e.g. v1.3.0; "" clears), 'admin_response' (public team reply shown on the board), 'title', 'description'. Omitted fields keep their value. Status changes are visible on the public board immediately: Planned/Started/Completed ideas form the public roadmap, Pending and Rejected are hidden. No emails are sent. The first time an idea moves to Completed, SeggWat auto-creates a DRAFT changelog entry for it (source completed_idea, once per idea — re-completing never duplicates it): title = idea title, body = admin_response if set, else the description, version = completed_in_version, component taken from an idea tag whose slug matches a changelog component. The draft is built from the values at that moment, so pass completed_in_version and admin_response in the same call as status Completed. The draft is never published automatically: review it with list_changelog / update_changelog_entry and publish with set_changelog_status. Returns the updated idea.

status.description: New status: Pending, Open, Planned, Started, Completed, Declined, Rejected (use merge_ideas for duplicates)

admin_response.description: Public team response shown on the board next to the idea

completed_in_version.description: Version the idea shipped in, e.g. "v1.3.0" (pass "" to clear)

catalog.name: verify_setup
catalog.description: Has this project received its first submission from a widget yet? `waiting` with a hint until it has, then `receiving` with the time of the first one.

since.description:
Only count events at or after this time. The agent passes the time it
called `setup_*`, so a reused resource's old events do not verify a
new install.

catalog.name: get_demo
catalog.description: Get one demo in full: metadata, publish state, and every step with its screenshot URL and annotations.

demo_id.description: The demo ID (as shown by list_demos)

catalog.name: get_demo_analytics
catalog.description: Get a demo's viewer analytics over a time window: total views, unique visitors, views per day, per-step completion rates (derive drop-off from these), and average time per step.

demo_id.description: The demo ID (as shown by list_demos)

catalog.name: get_workspace_analytics
catalog.description: Get workspace-wide analytics over a time window: total views and visitors across all demos, plus per-demo performance — the dashboard overview as data.

catalog.name: list_demos
catalog.description: List your demos: id, title, step count, public/private state, view count, folder, and type. Start here to find demo IDs for the other tools.

catalog.name: list_tours

catalog.name: set_demo_public
catalog.description: Publish or unpublish a demo. Publishing makes the share link and embeds publicly viewable; unpublishing hides them. Idempotent.

public.description: true to publish the demo (public share link + embeds), false to unpublish

demo_id.description: The demo ID (as shown by list_demos)

catalog.name: ack_triage
catalog.description: Mark a claimed triage item done so it is not handed out again. Idempotent.

catalog.name: claim_triage
catalog.description: Take issues off the triage queue. Claimed items are hidden from other agents until the lease expires, so the same issue is not diagnosed twice. Each item carries the release the error came from — check out that revision before reading the code. A regression also carries regressed_from_release, the release the fix was verified against: `git diff <regressed_from_release>..<release>` is the change set that reintroduced the bug. Call ack_triage when done.

level.description: Only issues at this level, e.g. `error`.

lease_seconds.description: How long the claim holds before the work is offered to someone else. Default 900.

catalog.name: create_project
catalog.description: Create a project and return the DSN to configure an SDK with. The DSN's public key is not a secret — it only grants the ability to send events to this project.

name.description: Display name. Defaults to the slug.

slug.description: URL-safe identifier used in API paths: letters, digits, '-' and '_'.

catalog.name: fix_record
catalog.description: What became of the fixes agents proposed: every analysis carrying a fix_url, graded against production, plus a per-agent tally. A fix is `held` when releases shipped after it was proposed and the issue was seen in none of them, `regressed` when the issue came back in a release that first appeared after it, and `pending` while nothing has shipped since. Read your own record here before trusting your own confidence.

limit.description: Max fixes to return, newest first. Capped at 200.

project.description: Restrict to one project. Omit for every project.

catalog.name: get_event
catalog.description: Fetch one event by the id the SDK assigned it, which is the id that appears in application logs.

event_id.description: The event id the SDK assigned, as it appears in application logs.

catalog.name: get_issue
catalog.description: Everything needed to diagnose one issue in a single call: the exception chain, every stack frame with its source context, breadcrumbs, runtime contexts, and any analysis already posted by another agent. For a regression, regressed_from_release is the last known good — `git diff <regressed_from_release>..<latest release>` is the change set that reintroduced the bug.

catalog.name: list_issues
catalog.description: List issues in a project, each with a 24-hour sparkline. Sorted by most recent activity by default; pass sort=events for the highest-volume issues first, which is usually what you want when deciding what to fix, or sort=users for the issues hitting the most distinct users. Filter with environment=production or tag=key:value. Returns titles, culprits and counts — use get_issue for the stack trace.

tag.description:
`key:value` — only issues with events carrying this tag, e.g. `server_name:web-3`
or `component:worker` (events ingested through a labeled DSN key).

sort.description: `events` for the highest-volume issues first, `users` for the most distinct users hit, `last_seen` (default) for the most recent.

limit.description: Max issues to return. Capped at 100.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the issue title.

environment.description: Only issues with events in this environment, e.g. `production`.

catalog.name: list_monitors
catalog.description: Cron monitors of a project: each scheduled job's schedule, last check-in and current status (ok, error, missed or timeout). A job that misses a run or overruns becomes an ordinary error event automatically; this answers "are my scheduled jobs healthy" before that happens. Monitors are created by the jobs themselves via Sentry check-ins, so an empty list means no job is instrumented.

catalog.name: list_projects
catalog.description: List projects reporting errors to Thermite, with their unresolved issue count and events in the last 24 hours.

catalog.name: pending_triage
catalog.description: See which issues are waiting for triage without taking them. Use claim_triage to actually pick work up.

level.description: Only issues at this level, e.g. `error`.

lease_seconds.description: How long the claim holds before the work is offered to someone else. Default 900.

catalog.name: post_analysis
catalog.description: Write a diagnosis back onto an issue so it is waiting for whoever opens it next. This is how triage work is preserved — without it the analysis is lost when the run ends. If you also opened a pull request for the fix, pass its URL as fix_url and it is shown alongside the diagnosis.

fix_url.description:
The pull request you opened for this issue, if you got that far. Must be on the same host
as the project's `repo_url`, which the triage item and `get_issue` both carry. Opening it
is your job — thermite holds no git credential and never calls the host.

release.description: The revision this was reasoned against, so a reader can tell if it is still current.

confidence.description: `high`, `medium` or `low`. Say low rather than guessing confidently.

catalog.name: project_stats
catalog.description: Error rate over time plus the current state of a project: events per bucket by level, unresolved issues, new issues and regressions.

catalog.name: release_health
catalog.description: Release health: how many sessions each recent release served and how many crashed, newest release first. Use this to tell a release that is broken from one that is merely busy — an error count alone cannot, because it rises with traffic. crash_free_rate is null below 50 sessions, where the rate would be noise. Requires an SDK with release health enabled; empty otherwise.

catalog.name: set_issue_status
catalog.description: Resolve, ignore or reopen an issue. Resolving is not final: a resolved issue that happens again is reopened and queued as a regression — pass in_next_release=true after fixing a bug whose fix has not shipped, so lingering traffic from already-seen releases does not reopen it. Ignoring is what suppresses an issue for good.

in_next_release.description:
With `resolved`: stay resolved for events from releases already seen (the broken deploy
still out there), and reopen as a regression only when a newer release reports the error.
Use after fixing a bug whose fix has not shipped yet. Requires the SDK to send a release.

catalog.name: setup_project
